problem: Sparse Bayesian Learning with automatic relevance determination is sensitive to data contaminations like outliers and misspecified noise, degrading model fit and predictions.
approach: Jointly learn individual feature and sample relevancies via a single Bayesian objective, enabling simultaneous model and data sparsification through automatic relevance determination extended to both model and data dimensions.
contribution: A symmetric pruning approach that jointly optimizes feature and sample sparsity via marginal likelihood, achieving robust and sparse prediction models across diverse regression tasks.

problem: Data Shapley-based selection sometimes performs no better than random selection, raising questions about when Shapley-based approaches work well and how to reliably identify high-quality data subsets.
approach: Decompose the utility function into simpler Shapley-informative components and aggregate them non-linearly via a framework called NASH that strategically leverages settings where Shapley values are most informative.
contribution: NASH substantially improves the effectiveness of Shapley-based data selection with minimal computational overhead by identifying and exploiting Shapley-informative components.

problem: Large language models suffer from high storage and runtime costs due to massive KV caches in transformers, and existing KV cache pruning methods lack formal theoretical grounding.
approach: Formally analyze output perturbation when removing KV cache entries and develop a perturbation-constrained selection algorithm that identifies critical entries by measuring worst-case perturbation impact.
contribution: A plug-and-play algorithm that reduces compression loss by more than half on average across 29 datasets when integrated with state-of-the-art cache eviction methods on three LLMs.

problem: Parameter sharing for model compression often causes severe accuracy degradation at high compression ratios because existing methods ignore the geometric properties of the loss landscape.
approach: Leverage Hessian eigenspace information to group layers with similar curvature profiles and align parameter sharing perturbations with low-curvature directions via curvature-aware graph coloring.
contribution: Achieve 28-50% parameter compression with negligible accuracy loss on LLaMA-7B and Swin Transformer while delivering over 60% higher inference throughput than prior methods.

problem: Reinforcement learning with sparse terminal rewards is sample-inefficient; textual feedback helps but treating it as fixed misses that feedback quality depends on the policy's ability to learn from it.
approach: Formulate learnable textual feedback for RL as a bilevel Stackelberg program and derive Bilevel Natural Language Actor-Critic (Bi-NAC) that jointly trains a critic to generate reward-improving feedback and an actor to exploit it.
contribution: 2B and 6B models outperform 3B and 7B GRPO baselines on MATH-500 and GPQA with improved sample and parameter efficiency through joint feedback-policy optimization.

problem: Low-light video enhancement with multimodal approaches assumes auxiliary modalities (event streams, infrared) are always available, which is infeasible in real-world scenarios.
approach: Propose AMNet with a Spatial-Spectral Dual-Gated Translator that learns correspondence between modalities and generates implicit auxiliary representations when modalities are absent, enabled by synthetic pretraining.
contribution: A unified framework supporting flexible modality-agnostic inference that handles arbitrary combinations of available modalities with superior LLVE performance under modality absence.

problem: Predictive Coding in digital simulation suffers from exponential signal decay that stalls the numerical process, limiting scalability to deeper architectures despite its brain-inspired appeal.
approach: Introduce error-based PC (ePC), a reparameterization that eliminates signal decay while numerically computing exact PC weight gradients orders of magnitude faster than state-based formulations.
contribution: ePC matches backpropagation performance even on deeper models where state-based PC struggles, enabling PC to scale in digital simulation with practical speedups.

problem: Multi-disease modeling in electronic health records lacks interpretability and principled uncertainty quantification; existing approaches either treat diseases independently or rely on opaque black-box architectures.
approach: Introduce a Bayesian hypergraph inference framework where risk factors act on hyperedges representing latent disease pathways, with a repulsion prior for parsimony and structured variational inference for scalability.
contribution: Stable and interpretable disease pathway structures with well-calibrated uncertainty, improved rare-disease estimation, and competitive predictive performance on UK Biobank EHR data.

problem: Unified drone-based object detectors using Mixture-of-Experts face performance imbalance across tasks due to uneven multi-task data distribution, causing over/under-activation of experts.
approach: Extend DINO with heterogeneous routed MoEs organized into shared, task-specific, and dynamic expert groups, and introduce task-recognition auxiliary training to ensure proper routing and feature discriminability.
contribution: DroneDINO consistently outperforms unified and task-specific detectors across multiple drone-based detection benchmarks with balanced expert activation.

problem: Protein language models can identify repeats in sequences, but the internal mechanisms behind this ability remain unclear, limiting understanding of how they solve biological pattern-matching tasks.
approach: Investigate PLM mechanisms for exact and approximate repeat detection by analyzing feature representations, positional attention heads, and induction heads that attend to aligned tokens across repeated segments.
contribution: Reveal that PLMs detect approximate repeats via a two-stage mechanism combining positional attention and biologically specialized components with induction-head cross-segment alignment.

problem: Understanding multi-agent interactions between language models is underexplored; it is unclear how representational similarity affects cooperation versus creativity in artificial agent interactions.
approach: Examine interaction patterns across 276 LLM pairs playing eight games spanning cooperation and novelty, measuring representational similarity at different model layers and its effects on behavioral outcomes.
contribution: Similar representation spaces drive higher cooperation but reduce novelty and creativity; similarity in early layers shows strongest association with these dynamics, suggesting shared lexical grounding as a key factor.

problem: Understanding how transformers learn sparse attention patterns and achieve head specialization during training remains unclear, particularly on tasks requiring selective integration of information from multiple positions.
approach: Study transformers on a Markov chain task and model attention learning dynamics via differential equations, revealing competitive and cooperative learning phases aligned with increasing model expressivity.
contribution: Prove stage-wise convergence of attention learning and characterize how sparse attention patterns and head specialization emerge incrementally without explicit curriculum, with implications for sequential task generalization.

problem: Direct alignment of LLMs with multiple conflicting human objectives fails because weighted loss methods cannot identify directions that improve all objectives simultaneously, and multi-objective methods rely on explicit reward models.
approach: Propose RACO, a reward-free framework that directly uses pairwise preference data and resolves gradient conflicts via a clipped variant of conflict-averse gradient descent with convergence guarantees to Pareto-critical points.
contribution: Consistently achieves better Pareto trade-offs than multi-objective baselines on summarization and safety alignment across multiple LLM families without explicit reward models.

problem: Neural logistic bandits face unfavorable dependencies on variance parameters and suffer from direct dependence on feature dimension, limiting scalability in high-dimensional neural settings.
approach: Introduce a Bernstein-type inequality for self-normalized vector-valued martingales that bypasses direct dimension dependence, then propose algorithms NeuralLog-UCB-1 and NeuralLog-UCB-2 based on this concentration result.
contribution: Regret bounds growing with effective dimension rather than ambient dimension: O-tilde(d-eff sqrt(kappa T)) and O-tilde(d-eff sqrt(T/kappa)), improving on existing results with minimal kappa dependence.

problem: Defenses against indirect prompt injection in LLMs typically suppress untrusted text to prevent attacks, but this corrupts legitimate tasks like translation and document editing that require preserving injected content.
approach: Introduce SecFid benchmark distinguishing between executing, processing, and ignoring injections, then measure the security-fidelity frontier across 1,168 examples and 48 configurations to expose hidden trade-offs.
contribution: Demonstrate a fundamental frontier where no model or defense achieves both objectives; most secure defenses reach 99.3% security at only 71.0-73.9% fidelity, highlighting the cost of security-focused approaches.

problem: Multi-modal point cloud completion relies on auxiliary modalities but standard hard projection produces sparse image-plane support, severing cross-modal connections and hindering visual prior propagation.
approach: Replace hard projection with differentiable Gaussian splatting to produce dense continuous image representations, reformulating projection as density estimation to avoid support collapse and improve gradient flow.
contribution: SplAttN achieves state-of-the-art performance on PCN and ShapeNet benchmarks and maintains robust visual dependence on KITTI, validating effective cross-modal connection unlike baselines that degenerate to unimodal template retrieval.

problem: Sequential conditional independence tests typically require exact knowledge of Model-X conditionals, making them fragile when the conditional distribution must be estimated rather than known exactly.
approach: Apply testing-by-betting to an adaptively optimized Kernel Conditional Independence statistic with normalization and truncate-and-shift calibration to reduce Type I error inflation from estimation error.
contribution: Substantially more robust to Model-X estimation error than existing sequential tests while preserving high power across synthetic benchmarks and real-world fairness tasks, outperforming prior sequential approaches.

problem: Training diffusion and flow policies in online RL is difficult because there are no direct samples from the target Boltzmann distribution; existing methods use either noise or gradient expectations as training targets with unclear relationships.
approach: Formulate RFM as a reverse inference problem and introduce Langevin Stein operators to construct zero-mean control variates, unifying noise-expectation and gradient-expectation methods in a broader class of estimators.
contribution: A unified framework extending Boltzmann distribution targeting from diffusion to flow policies and enabling principled design of training objectives for RL with generative models.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle with long-horizon non-Markovian tasks requiring long-term memory and reasoning, facing a frequency-competence paradox where high-performance models are too slow for real-time control.
approach: Introduce HiMe, a hierarchical framework decoupling embodied intelligence into a high-frequency Executor, a Sentry for working memory, and a Planner for long-term strategy, with dynamic knowledge using cross-modal semantic schemas.
contribution: Significantly improves long-horizon task success rates while balancing real-time execution and deliberative planning, with the ability to self-correct internal knowledge based on human preferences.

problem: Converting Rényi Differential Privacy profiles to hypothesis-testing trade-offs lacks a known optimal rule; existing conversions may be suboptimal for some RDP profiles or error levels.
approach: Prove that the intersection-of-RDP-privacy-regions rule is optimal by providing a precise geometric characterization of RDP privacy regions and showing boundary determination by Bernoulli mechanisms.
contribution: Establish that the intersection rule achieves optimal bounds uniformly for all RDP profiles and Type I error levels, marking the fundamental limit of what can be inferred from RDP guarantees alone.

problem: Vision-language models rely on textual shortcuts and underutilize visual evidence during reasoning; RL applications to VLMs are hindered by lack of scalable, reliable reward signals.
approach: Propose SSL4RL, reformulating self-supervised learning objectives (rotation prediction, patch reconstruction) into dense automatic rewards for RL without requiring human preferences or AI evaluators.
contribution: Substantially improves performance on vision-centric and vision-language benchmarks with greater resilience to visual corruptions; systematic ablations identify key design factors for SSL-based reward functions.

problem: Flow-based generative models excel at capturing complex distributions but are underexplored for representation learning and resolving fine-grained structural details beyond generation.
approach: Show that rectified flow exhibits zero-flow at t=0.5 iff source and target distributions are identical (zero-flow criterion), then translate this into a simulation-free loss for learning amortized Markov blankets and representations.
contribution: Demonstrate zero-flow encoders' effectiveness on learning latent representations and certifying conditional independence for both synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Long-video generation with Diffusion Transformers faces prohibitive quadratic attention costs; sparse attention helps but struggles with non-sparse heads, limiting speed-quality trade-offs.
approach: Identify frame-block similarity redundancy in video DiTs where attention weight distributions are highly similar across frames, then propose EchoAttention combining sparse operators with lightweight linear calibration and learned routing.
contribution: Consistently improve speed-quality frontier across video DiTs, reducing end-to-end latency up to 2.42x with minimal quality loss through joint token-pair and frame-block redundancy exploitation.

problem: Understanding why neural networks generalize well on natural data requires examining inductive biases; natural data's learnability is hypothesized to stem from physical constraints like symmetry and locality.
approach: Use 2D cellular automata as controlled testbed with perfect locality and symmetry, examining smoothness and circuit complexity via junta coefficients measuring Fourier weight concentration by interaction degree.
contribution: Find that locality and symmetry alone are insufficient; learnable functions concentrate spectral weight at low degrees with low circuit complexity, supporting hypothesis that natural data's learnability comes from low interaction complexity.

problem: Large vision-language models struggle with precise alignment between visual components and textual descriptions, and their reasoning can be improved by external visual cues that structure the modalities.
approach: Show that external cues (symbols, grid lines) create latent Grounding IDs that arise within the model, forming identifiers that enhance alignment between visual and text representations.
contribution: Grounding IDs improve cross-modal alignment, reduce hallucinations, and enhance attention between related components, demonstrating that external cues are a key mechanism for improving LVLM multimodal reasoning.

problem: Evaluating conditional coverage of conformal prediction sets is challenging; existing metrics suffer from sample inefficiency, overfitting, and lack power to detect coverage violations.
approach: Cast conditional coverage estimation as a classification problem where violations occur iff some classifier achieves lower risk than target; derive excess risk of target coverage (ERT) via proper loss functions.
contribution: ERT provides conservative estimates of coverage miscoverage measures with higher statistical power than established metrics like CovGap, with an open-source implementation and benchmark across conformal methods.

problem: Medical image segmentation models achieve strong performance but remain opaque, limiting diagnosis of failures, understanding of dataset shift, and principled intervention strategies.
approach: Introduce Med-SegLens, a model-diffing framework decomposing segmentation activations into interpretable latent features using sparse autoencoders, enabling cross-architecture and cross-dataset latent alignment.
contribution: Identify latent features as causal bottlenecks for failures and show targeted interventions correct 70% of errors, improving Dice score from 39.4% to 74.2% without retraining.

problem: Multi-view generation is dominated by continuous diffusion approaches; discrete diffusion's potential for this task and its ability to unify language-vision modeling remains unexplored.
approach: Formulate multi-view generation as discrete sequence modeling with visual tokens from MAGVIT-v2, using discrete diffusion via masked token prediction with self-attention for cross-view consistency.
contribution: ViewMask-1-to-3 outperforms baselines on GSO and 3D-FUTURE benchmarks with 10.6% higher IoU than continuous diffusion models while naturally extending to text-to-image and multimodal understanding.

problem: Large language models display comprehensive abilities, but the internal mechanisms supporting these behaviors are insufficiently understood, limiting interpretability and targeted improvement.
approach: Identify keystone neurons—a sparse subset consistently highly activated across tasks—whose removal causes behavior collapse and whose parameters are tightly calibrated during training.
contribution: Show that fine-tuning only keystone neurons achieves task gains comparable to or better than full-parameter fine-tuning while better preserving performance on other capability dimensions.

problem: Online covering problems lack simple frameworks to rigorously incorporate learned predictions; existing approaches don't provide clear guarantees that improve with prediction accuracy.
approach: Propose a general framework turning any online algorithm with competitive ratio ρ(k, ·) into one with ratio ρ(η, ·) where η is prediction error, via black-box transformation.
contribution: A universal framework applicable to facility location, Steiner problems, set cover, and parking permits that breaks worst-case lower bounds with accurate predictions and gracefully degrades with error.

problem: Large-scale grading of handwritten mathematics in STEM courses requires evaluating complex reasoning and partial credit; AI grading reliability on real handwritten work remains unvalidated.
approach: Deploy OCR-conditioned LLMs with structured rubric-guided prompting to grade thousands of real handwritten calculus quiz submissions and evaluate against TA grades, surveys, and independent human review.
contribution: Demonstrate strong alignment with official TA scoring and acceptable AI-generated feedback quality; identify key failure modes and propose practical rubric/prompt-design principles for reliable real-course deployment.

problem: In retrieval-augmented generation, LLMs may fail to utilize query-relevant content from retrieved evidence, shifting focus toward assessing contextual grounding rather than generic uncertainty quantification.
approach: Use information flow to trace each context token's layer-wise contribution to output, then introduce simulatability and concentration metrics to assess whether predictions align with true token relevance and derive from focused subsets.
contribution: Achieve average AUROC of 0.709, exceeding runner-up 0.676, for uncertainty estimation in RAG while maintaining moderate computational cost via layer-wise information flow analysis.

problem: Multi-hop fact verification requires complex reasoning across evidence; LLMs suffer from hallucinations and fractured logical chains despite Chain-of-Thought attempts to improve transparency.
approach: Ground reasoning in explicit directed dependency graphs inspired by structural causal models, treating verification as constructive structural reasoning, and optimize via Group Relative Policy Optimization to balance depth versus conciseness.
contribution: SCM-GRPO outperforms strong baselines on HoVer and EX-FEVER with more traceable reasoning structures, revealing inverted U-shaped correlation between reasoning-chain length and accuracy.

problem: Abundant open-source model repositories lack adequate documentation; weight-space learning could identify models from parameters alone, but processing full-scale weights is prohibitive.
approach: Introduce MVProbe, a multi-perspective probing framework synthesizing first-order signals with interaction-aware Gram-based views, with principled standardization ensuring balanced contributions across probing orders.
contribution: Consistently outperforms ProbeX across ResNet, SupViT, MAE, and DINO architectures by capturing higher-order correlation patterns in weight interactions through multi-view probing.

problem: Real-world datasets feature skewed class distributions and noisy annotations; active learning for such data lacks principled methods to balance sample selection across imbalanced, noisy labels.
approach: Propose an active learning framework with foundation model priors enabling imbalance-aware co-decisions between foundation and small models, systematically exploring the dual challenges of label noise and class imbalance.
contribution: Achieve over 50% annotation savings compared to best baselines while preserving performance and robustness to label noise across imbalanced image and text datasets.

problem: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by KV cache memory demands; self-speculative decoding with sparse attention improves throughput but uses standalone KV selection algorithms that miss criticality computed during verification.
approach: Propose Vegas, identifying critical KV entries as a byproduct of verification and using these entries for sparse attention drafting in subsequent tokens, reducing KV selection overhead.
contribution: Achieve 1.25x-2.81x speedup over vLLM and 1.15x-1.29x speedup over state-of-the-art sparse-attention self-speculative methods by leveraging verification-guided KV selection.

problem: Sampling discrete compositional objects from posteriors can be solved by learning MDPs, but the Markovian assumption hampers signal propagation and reduces expressivity through state aliasing.
approach: Lift MDP learning with path-dependent latent dynamics allowing the policy to depend on entire trajectory history rather than current state alone, extending amortized inference algorithms to this setting.
contribution: Path-dependent discrete amortized inference often achieves faster convergence and improved state space exploration on standard benchmark problems versus prior Markovian approaches.

problem: Fairness in real-world decision systems requires multi-stage multi-agent reasoning where disparities accumulate over time; existing fairness methods operating at isolated decision points fail to address dynamic, systemic inequities.
approach: Introduce MAFE, a suite of open-source multi-agent fair environments supporting heterogeneous agents, configurable interventions, and fairness metrics compatible with standard MARL libraries.
contribution: Enable reproducible evaluation of fairness-aware policies and reveal critical trade-offs between fairness, performance, and coordination through experiments on loan processing, healthcare, and education.

problem: LLM preference alignment methods treat truthfulness and helpfulness as universally collaborative or conflicting across all samples, missing that these objectives conflict in only a small subset.
approach: Propose CAMP, which explicitly models when conflicts arise and adaptively regulates optimization strength based on sample-specific conflict detection, balancing truthfulness and helpfulness.
contribution: Consistently improve truthfulness while maintaining favorable helpfulness compared to hallucination mitigation and multi-objective baselines through adaptive conflict-aware margin preference alignment.

problem: Benchmarking LLMs by evaluating every model on every query is wasteful; early stopping rules can reduce costs but haven't exploited the property that models respond similarly to the same prompt.
approach: Propose Synchronized Successive Rejects (SySRs), augmenting the classical Successive Reject algorithm with paired comparisons, hyperparameter-free with guarantees improving with model similarity.
contribution: Outperforms all baselines on 15 benchmarks in average error rate and worst-case budget for identifying the best model by leveraging response similarity without hyperparameter tuning.
